chapter: Child's, teaching and the Village (corrected typing)
title: Teaching: forty pupils then four, and teaching the blues
summary: Hodes began teaching when jobs were scarce and got to forty pupils before tiring. Today he takes four, and he says he teaches the blues to anyone who can whistle.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: That's -- at that same time Ira Sullivan was selling clothes at some men's shop in I think Rothschilds in Park Forest.
You were talking about selling pianos and --

Yeah, I didn't volunteer, but I was teaching. And one day I looked at my hands and I says, well, you might as well give them away. They're not doing anything good. And the says, well, that's an idea, why don't you teach? You can do that if you can't find jobs. You can teach, you might as well do something with them.

And I started to teach. I got up to where I got about 40 pupils before I got sick of teaching, because I realized what I was doing was waiting for a lunch break or waiting for a smoke break or waiting for a coffee break, that I had too many people, I couldn't get interested in that many. It was more of an accumulation, of making a living out of it. And thats a different thing. So today, when I teach, I might have four people in a week. And I know each one of them, and I can say I'm going away to work, because this is not work, this is like gardening. Although you pay me, it's still like gardening, and I want to keep it that way.

But then, it was a different matter. But, anyway, getting back to New York, I did do some accidental teaching in New York, because always somebody came along and says, you play so simple in effect, is what they said to me. And I think you could teach me how to play. And I would say, if you

can whistle, I can teach you how to play the blues. You want to play the blues? If you can whistle, you can hear a note, I can show you with one finger, I can show you a bass. And we'll sit down and have some fun.
